2027-03-15.title: Monday of the sixth week of the Great Fast
readings: Abraham sends his servant to find a wife for Isaac
Pray in the Spirit at all times; an ambassador in chains
“By what authority are you doing these things?”
2027-03-15.alt: Great Fast (Valiya Nombu), sixth week. The last full week of the Forty Days: the Fortieth Friday is 19 March, Lazarus Saturday 20 March, and Hosanna Sunday 21 March.
2027-03-15.verse: Pray in the Spirit at all times in every prayer and supplication. To that end keep alert and always persevere in supplication for all the saints.
theo: This week the readings from Genesis follow one long and lovely story: how Abraham's servant went to find a bride for Isaac. It begins today with an old man settling his affairs. “Now Abraham was old, well advanced in years; and the Lord had blessed Abraham in all things.” He calls the oldest servant of his house and makes him swear that he will not take a wife for Isaac from the Canaanites around them, but will go back to Abraham's own kindred. The servant raises an honest difficulty: what if the woman will not come? Abraham's answer is the answer of a man who has walked with God for a lifetime: “The Lord, the God of heaven, who took me from my father’s house and from the land of my birth, and who spoke to me and swore to me, ‘To your offspring I will give this land,’ he will send his angel before you.” Abraham cannot see how it will work out; he only knows who has been faithful to him. The promise of descendants as many as the stars depends on this one marriage, and Abraham entrusts it to God. Isaac must not go back: the family of promise looks forward, not backward.

Paul, writing from prison, asks the Ephesians for the same trust expressed as prayer: “Pray in the Spirit at all times in every prayer and supplication. To that end keep alert and always persevere in supplication for all the saints.” He calls himself “an ambassador in chains,” and asks them to pray that he may speak the mystery of the gospel boldly. In the Gospel Jesus stands in the Temple in the last days before his Passion, and the authorities demand: “By what authority are you doing these things? Who gave you this authority to do them?” Jesus answers with a question about John the Baptist, and they will not answer, not because they do not know, but because they fear the crowd. St John Chrysostom remarked that the Lord does not hide the truth from those who seek it, but he does not cast it before those who ask only to trap him (in substance). As the Forty Days draw to a close, the Church asks us whether we come to Jesus to argue or to obey. His authority is the authority of the Son, and in a few days it will be shown most clearly on the Cross.
outline: Ask: when you cannot see the way ahead, whom do you trust?
Point 1 · He will send his angel before you
Abraham trusts the God who has been faithful.
An ambassador in chains asks for prayer.
Coming to Jesus to obey, not to argue.
“Pray in the Spirit at all times.”
live: Name one decision that worries you, and give it to God in prayer each morning this week.
Pray every day this week for one priest or missionary by name, that he or she may speak the gospel boldly.
2027-03-15.prayer: Lord God of heaven and earth, you led Abraham from his father's house and sent your angel before his servant. Go before us in the choices we must make, and teach us to trust you where we cannot see. Keep us alert and persevering in prayer for all your saints, and give courage to all who proclaim your gospel, especially those in chains. Let us come to your Son not to argue but to obey, as we follow him to Jerusalem. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
altar: Abraham trusted that God would provide; at the altar the Father gives us the Bridegroom himself, the Son with all authority, given for the life of the world.

quick: Old Abraham sends his servant to find a wife for Isaac, trusting God to send his angel ahead.
Paul, an ambassador in chains, asks for prayer at all times.
Jesus is asked by what authority he acts; his questioners will not answer the truth they fear.
2027-03-15.action: Give one worrying decision to God in prayer this morning.
2027-03-15.question: Do I come to Jesus to obey him, or to argue with him?

family.explain: Abraham was very old. He wanted a good wife for his son Isaac, so he sent his most trusted servant on a long journey. The servant was worried, but Abraham said: God will send his angel before you. Abraham could not see the future, but he knew God had always looked after him.
family.intention: We pray for young people who are choosing their path in life.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one thing we are worried about, that we can give to God together tonight?”

illus: An old man in Kottayam, a retired schoolteacher, kept a small diary of answered prayers. When his grandson was anxious about where to study, the old man did not give advice at first. He opened the diary and read out, year by year, the things he had once worried about and how God had carried the family through each one. Then he closed it and said: I do not know what will happen to you. I only know who has been faithful to us. The boy said later that this did more for him than any counsel.

pm.open: Lord God, you go before us. Make us alert and persevering in prayer, and teach us to trust you where we cannot see. Amen.
share: He will send his angel before you (Genesis 24:7). Where do I need to trust that God goes before me?
Pray in the Spirit at all times (Ephesians 6:18). How faithful is my daily prayer in these last days of the Fast?
They were afraid of the crowd (Mark 11:32). When has fear of others kept me from saying what I know is true?
interc: For young people discerning marriage, priesthood or religious life.
For priests, catechists and missionaries, that they may proclaim the gospel boldly.
For Christians imprisoned for their faith, ambassadors in chains.
For the elderly, that they may hand on their faith with trust.
For all of us, that we may finish the Forty Days in faithful prayer.
pm.close: Father, you were faithful to Abraham in his old age and you hear the prayer of your Church. Go before us, keep us alert in prayer, and give us the courage to acknowledge the authority of your Son. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, this week we follow a beautiful story in Genesis. Abraham is old, and he sends his trusted servant to find a wife for his son Isaac. The servant is worried: what if the woman will not come? Abraham says: The Lord, the God of heaven, he will send his angel before you (Genesis 24:7).
Abraham does not know how it will work out. He only knows that God has been faithful to him all his life. That is the faith we need too. We do not see the future, but we know the God who holds it.

Paul, writing from prison, asks: Pray in the Spirit at all times in every prayer and supplication (Ephesians 6:18). He calls himself an ambassador in chains. Prayer is how we keep trusting when the way is hard.

In the Gospel the leaders ask Jesus: By what authority are you doing these things? (Mark 11:28). They are not seeking the truth; they fear the crowd. In these last days of the Fast, let us come to Jesus not to argue but to obey, for his authority is the love that will lead him to the Cross. Amen.
kids: Children, Abraham sent his servant on a long journey, and he told him: God will send his angel before you. When you go somewhere new, to a new class or a new place, remember: God goes ahead of you. You can say: Jesus, go before me today.

intro: Theme: “Pray in the Spirit at all times.”
As the Forty Days draw to a close: the God who goes before us, the prayer that never stops, and the authority of the Son.

points.h: He will send his angel before you
sub: The God who has been faithful.
q: I am going to send an angel in front of you, to guard you on the way and to bring you to the place that I have prepared.
By faith Abraham obeyed when he was called to set out for a place that he was to receive as an inheritance; and he set out, not knowing where he was going.
points.apply: Give one decision about the future to God each morning this week.

q: Let my prayer be counted as incense before you, and the lifting up of my hands as an evening sacrifice.
Rejoice always, pray without ceasing, give thanks in all circumstances; for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus for you.
points.apply: Pray daily this week for one priest or missionary by name.

q: For a child has been born for us, a son given to us; authority rests upon his shoulders; and he is named Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.
And Jesus came and said to them, “All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to me.
points.apply: Bring one teaching of Jesus you find hard to him this week, not to argue but to obey.

concl: Abraham trusted the God he could not see; Paul prayed in chains.
The Son whose authority was questioned will show it on the Cross.
2027-03-15.resolve: Pray at all times in these last days of the Fast, and obey the Lord who goes before us.
